messages.subject_clean: ggtree with pie charts in facets
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am really glad with ggtree, but I get stuck with what I want to do. I hope that someone can help me here.

I would like to plot pie charts, that vary in size relative to the sample size and are already facetted, next to my tree. I hoped that facet_plot would work, but I am not able to make it work. I have the very simple code below and I am sorry but I am just lost. Plotting the tree and the pie-charts separately works, but I cannot get it working together. Thank you very much in advance for your help.

My best,
Setareh

test <- read.table("ETBiosynthesis_SyntelogsHomologsPercentages_180622.txt", header =TRUE)

tree <- read.tree("tree_nexus.txt")

blank_theme <- theme_minimal()+ theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),axis.title.y = element_blank(),panel.border = element_blank(),panel.grid=element_blank(),axis.ticks = element_blank(), plot.title=element_blank())

pie <- ggplot(test,aes(x=Size/2,y=Percentage,fill=Group,width = Size)) + geom_bar(position ="fill",stat="identity") + facet_grid(Species ~ PFAM) + coord_polar("y",start=0) + blank_theme + theme(axis.text.x=element_blank()) + scale_fill_manual(values=c("Syntelogs"='khaki2','Homologs'='black'))

facet_plot(boom,panel='bar',data=test,geom = geom_bar,aes(x=Size/2,y=Percentage,fill=Group,width = Size))

messages.subject: Re: geom_nodepoint by node number
messages.body_plain:
Dear Laura,

Check this vignette:
https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/ggtree/inst/doc/treeManipulation.html

But, as an starting point (using the attached tree):

#Load ggtree
library(ggtree)

# read your favorite beast, mrbayes, or newick tree with bootstrap support
my_loaded_tree <- read.beast(file="mytree.tre")

# Add a new field with "selected nodes"
my_loaded_tree@fields <- c(my_loaded_tree@fields, "my_selected_node_column")

# Mark everyone as "non_selected
my_loaded_tree@stats$my_selected_node_column <- "non_selected"

# In my case, "prob_percent" is the posterior probability.
# Just tag nodes with more than 90 percent:
my_loaded_tree@stats$my_selected_node_column[my_loaded_tree@stats$prob_percent > 90] <- "selected"

# my "regular" tree
mytree <- ggtree(my_loaded_tree)

# my tree with nodepoint color by selection
mytree + geom_nodepoint(aes(colour=my_selected_node_column), size=2)

# :)

On Tue, Jun 26, 2018 at 8:21 AM, Douglas Adamoski <douglas....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dear Laura,
>

>

>
> # Mark everyone as "non_selected

>
> # In my case, "prob_percent" is the posterior probability.
> # Just tag nodes with more than 90 percent:
> my_loaded_tree@stats$my_selected_node_column[my_loaded_tree@stats$prob_percent > 90] <- "selected"
>
> # my "regular" tree
> mytree <- ggtree(my_loaded_tree)
>
> # my tree with nodepoint color by selection
> mytree + geom_nodepoint(aes(colour=my_selected_node_column), size=2)
>
> # :)
>

thanks for your sharing. However you are not using the latest ggtree. Current version of ggtree rely on treeio and the output of read.beast is a treedata object, which doesn't have stats slot.

You can just use subset aesthetic:

ggtree(my_loaded_tree) + geom_nodepoint(aes(subset = prob_percent > 90))

which works for geom_nodepoint, geom_tippoint, geom_nodelab and geom_tiplab, etc.

> >
> > #Load ggtree
> > library(ggtree)
> >
> > # read your favorite beast, mrbayes, or newick tree with bootstrap support
> > my_loaded_tree <- read.beast(file="mytree.tre")
> >
> > # Add a new field with "selected nodes"
> > my_loaded_tree@fields <- c(my_loaded_tree@fields, "my_selected_node_column")
> >
> > # Mark everyone as "non_selected
> > my_loaded_tree@stats$my_selected_node_column <- "non_selected"
> >
> > # In my case, "prob_percent" is the posterior probability.
> > # Just tag nodes with more than 90 percent:
> > my_loaded_tree@stats$my_selected_node_column[my_loaded_tree@stats$prob_percent > 90] <- "selected"
> >
> > # my "regular" tree
> > mytree <- ggtree(my_loaded_tree)
> >
> > # my tree with nodepoint color by selection
> > mytree + geom_nodepoint(aes(colour=my_selected_node_column), size=2)
> >
> > # :)
> >
>
> thanks for your sharing. However you are not using the latest ggtree. Current version of ggtree rely on treeio and the output of read.beast is a treedata object, which doesn't have stats slot.
>
> You can just use subset aesthetic:
>
> ggtree(my_loaded_tree) + geom_nodepoint(aes(subset = prob_percent > 90))
>
>
> which works for geom_nodepoint, geom_tippoint, geom_nodelab and geom_tiplab, etc.
>
>
>
